blocks.text: 1. Encoder-Decoder Models

blocks.alt: An input sequence goes through an encoder and decoder to an output sequence

blocks.text: Decoder-Only Models, the previous topic, dropped the encoder for genuinely open-ended generation tasks. Encoder-Decoder Models keep both halves for tasks needing both understanding and generation, explored throughout this topic.
This is the genuinely full, original Transformer structure already covered throughout the previous module, now explored specifically as its own genuine architectural category.
2. Recapping The Two Specialized Families
This connects back to Encoder-Only Models and Decoder-Only Models, both already covered. Both prior topics genuinely dropped one half of the full Transformer to specialize.

Encoder-Decoder Models genuinely keep both halves together instead, the genuinely third, complete option already implicitly hinted at by the two specialized families already covered in the previous two topics.
3. Why Neither Half Alone Suffices

blocks.alt: Encoder-only has no generation while decoder-only is one-directional

blocks.text: This connects back to Sequence-to-Sequence Learning, already covered in its own topic. Some genuinely real tasks need both a genuinely deep understanding of the input and a genuinely flexible, sequential output.
Neither Encoder-Only nor Decoder-Only alone, both already covered, fully satisfies both needs at once, directly motivating the complete architecture explored throughout the rest of this topic.

5. Bidirectional Encoding, Causal Decoding

blocks.alt: A bidirectional encoder feeds a causal decoder

blocks.text: This connects back to bidirectional context and Causal Masking, both already covered. The encoder genuinely uses bidirectional Self-Attention; the decoder genuinely uses causal Self-Attention plus Cross-Attention.

This combines the genuinely best property of each specialized family already covered in the two previous topics, keeping bidirectional understanding on the input side and causal, sequential generation on the output side.

10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates a complete Encoder-Decoder Model pipeline, combining bidirectional encoding with causal, Cross-Attention-connected decoding, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 8

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

def encoder_layer(x, rng):
    # already covered as bidirectional encoding in this topic: no masking at all
    W_q, W_k, W_v = [rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1 for _ in range(3)]
    weights = softmax((x @ W_q.T) @ (x @ W_k.T).T / np.sqrt(hidden_size))
    return x + weights @ (x @ W_v.T)

def decoder_layer(x, encoder_output, rng):
    seq_len = x.shape[0]
    causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1).astype(bool)
    W_q, W_k, W_v = [rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1 for _ in range(3)]
    scores = (x @ W_q.T) @ (x @ W_k.T).T / np.sqrt(hidden_size)
    scores[causal_mask] = -np.inf
    x = x + softmax(scores) @ (x @ W_v.T)  # already covered as causal decoding in this topic

    Wc_q, Wc_k, Wc_v = [rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1 for _ in range(3)]
    cross_scores = (x @ Wc_q.T) @ (encoder_output @ Wc_k.T).T / np.sqrt(hidden_size)
    x = x + softmax(cross_scores) @ (encoder_output @ Wc_v.T)  # already covered as Cross-Attention connection
    return x

encoder_input = rng.normal(size=(5, hidden_size))
decoder_input = rng.normal(size=(3, hidden_size))

encoder_output = encoder_layer(encoder_input, rng)
decoder_output = decoder_layer(decoder_input, encoder_output, rng)

print(f"Encoder output shape (bidirectional, already covered): {encoder_output.shape}")
print(f"Decoder output shape (causal plus Cross-Attention, already covered): {decoder_output.shape}")

Some tasks need both deep understanding of input and flexible, sequential output.
This is the exact same complete structure already covered in Transformer Architecture.
The encoder uses bidirectional Self-Attention; the decoder uses causal Self-Attention plus Cross-Attention.
T5 and BART, covered in later topics of this module, are influential Encoder-Decoder Models.
Keeping both halves costs more parameters and computation than either specialized family alone.
